subject: Re: Veridian Consulting — MSA/DPA/SOW redlines and SLA carveouts
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@veridian.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Turner <mark.turner@veridian.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Veridian — initial redlines for MSA/DPA/SOW

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Per our legal review, please find attached the Veridian redlines for the MSA and the SOW (attachments). High-level items we flagged:

- Data processing: we marked standard DPA language and requested annual audit rights and a requirement to share the subprocessor list 30 days prior to onboarding.
- SLA: requesting 99.95% uptime for the connector and 4-hour P1 response window.
- IP/Deliverables: want explicit assignment for custom integration work described in the SOW.
- Indemnity: typical mutual carveouts but we proposed a 2x fee cap for third-party IP claims.

We also noted a number of operational asks in the SOW around runbook handoffs and a 3-month transition plan. Can you confirm if your standard MSA already limits audit scope and whether Redwood can support the requested SLA?

Attachments: Veridian_Redlines_v1.docx (docx), Veridian_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call this week.

— Elena

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@veridian.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian — initial redlines for MSA/DPA/SOW

Elena — thanks for the redlines and the clear callouts. Quick read-through and our initial positions below (attached: RW_MSA_Counters_v2.docx):

- SLA: We can support a 99.9% availability SLA for the hosted connector with a credit scheme; 99.95% would push into dedicated capacity pricing. If Veridian needs 99.95 we should discuss a dedicated capacity commitment in the SOW.
- Data processing / audit: standard practice at Redwood is to allow scoped audits (SOC2 evidence or compliance report) rather than full on-site audits. We’re open to annual compliance attestations but would ask to limit auditor access to systems that process Veridian data.
- Subprocessors: we will share an approved subprocessor list and provide 30 days’ notice for material changes. For cloud infra providers we publish the list in our security portal.
- Indemnity/cap: we typically cap liability at the greater of $1M or 1x fees in the prior 12 months for commercial deals. For IP claims we prefer mutual indemnity with a limited carveout for gross negligence and will not accept a 2x fee multiplier.
- IP for custom work: we can assign deliverable rights in the SOW for integration work; we need to clarify open-source component obligations.

Action items:
1) Legal (cc’d Marissa) — please review the attached counters and propose which clauses are negotiable versus non-starters.
2) Ben/Marissa — can you confirm cost delta for a 99.95% SLA and whether we need Dedicated for that?
3) Elena — if you can prioritize the SOW sections that require assignment vs. licensing, we’ll take that to the product/eng team for scope estimate.

Attachments: RW_MSA_Counters_v2.docx (docx)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
(650) 555-0110

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian — initial redlines for MSA/DPA/SOW

Kim / team — quick operational notes from my side after skimming the counters:

- SLA delta: 99.95% vs 99.9% is ~1.5–2x on infra cost depending on traffic profile. If they want 99.95 we should ask for a 12-month minimum committed throughput in the SOW (or move to Dedicated).
- Credits: propose a sliding credit cap (up to 50% of monthly fees) but keep overall liability cap separate.
- Audit: agree-with-Kimberly on scoped compliance evidence (SOC2 report + specific logs). If Veridian insists on on-site audits, add cost recovery and pre-approved scope.
- Subprocessors: we should make the list evergreen on a public URL rather than having to email PDFs back and forth.

One other ask: we should explicitly exclude any obligation to preserve raw model training data in the SOW — operations can't support indefinite retention. Mark this as non-negotiable.

Happy to draft an ops-focused concession matrix.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Elena Morales <elena@veridian.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Turner <mark.turner@veridian.com>, Veridian Consulting Legal <legal@veridian.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian — initial redlines for MSA/DPA/SOW

Kim, Ben — thanks for the quick responses and for the counters attached. A few follow-ups from Veridian legal after internal review:

- SLA: Veridian’s customers require a 99.95% SLA for the connector. We understand the cost implications; Mark is open to a committed usage tier in the SOW.
- Audit: our counsel prefers the option of an annual third-party audit with limited scope. If you can provide SOC2 + compliance packet and allow a 1x/year remote audit, that meets their risk committee.
- Indemnity: Veridian will not accept a cap below 2x fees for third-party IP claims — this is a deal driver for their legal team.
- Data residency & deletion: need guarantees around deletion timelines after contract termination (standard ask is 60 days for backups/logs) and proof via deletion report.

We can accept scoped auditor access (remote) instead of on-site. On the SLA we can consider a compromise: start at 99.9% for the first 6 months while integration stabilizes, then move to 99.95% after production sign-off and a committed throughput in the SOW.

DocuSign: we’ve dropped a redline envelope if you want to track versions: https://www.docusign.com/VERIDIAN-MSA-Envelope-12345

— Elena

Ben / Marcus, we need a short cost estimate for the 99.95% SLA + committed throughput model and a proposal for the deletion/reporting mechanism (who owns the deletion certificate + how we prove it).

I’ve started a concession matrix (attached) that maps ask -> our position -> risk level. Legal: please flag any non-starters — if Veridian insists on 2x IP cap we should decide if this is a term to escalate to leadership.

Attachments: Concession_Matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
